reader_question: How close is federal debt to the limit set in law?
grade_line: Documented: the Treasury’s monthly statement of the public debt
title: Federal debt subject to the limit stood at $40,327.1 billion on October 31, 2026, $776.9 billion under the $41,104.0 billion limit.
measure_line: Federal debt subject to the limit set in law, held by the public and by government accounts, against the limit, billions of dollars, nominal, October 31, 2026, United States
notes: Public Law 119-21, signed July 4, 2025, raised the limit by $5,000 billion, from $36,104.0 billion to $41,104.0 billion.
alt: A bullet graph of federal debt subject to the limit on October 31, 2026: a bar to $40,327.1 billion against a tick at the $41,104.0 billion limit, over a darker band to the earlier limit of $36,104.0 billion. The debt sits $776.9 billion under the limit.

table.caption: Federal debt subject to the limit and the limit, millions of dollars, October 31, 2026

columns.label: Debt subject to the limit, millions

chart_notes: The darker band runs to the limit in force from January to June 2025, $36,104.0 billion, and the lighter band on to the limit since July 2025, $41,104.0 billion, marked by a tick. The bar is the debt.
